question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

At your beck and call

options.text: To have absolute control over someone
To have no control over someone
To call someone and then deny

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase** 'At your beck and call'** means to be always ready to obey or serve someone, to be continually available to satisfy someone's demands.(आपकी हर आज्ञा का पालन करने के लिए तैयार)
 
• It **implies a situation **where you have absolute control over someone, as they are always ready to respond to your demands.
 
 
• **For example-** '*He expects his employees to be at his** beck and call **day and night.'*
 
 

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- *'To have absolute control over someone'.*
